llm.reply:
Li-Fraumeni syndrome is associated with tumor protein p53, NCBIGene:7157, and with checkpoint kinase 2, NCBIGene:11200, and with cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A, NCBIGene:1029, alongside the disease record itself, named Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2].

## Core Genetic Cause

The syndrome is described as a cancer predisposition condition caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern with high penetrance [19: "Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1"]. Loss of p53 function downstream of these mutations is described as permissive for the development of multiple malignancies across life [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53, leading to downstream events permissive for development of various malignancies throughout life"]. A confirmed case report likewise documented a germline TP53 mutation, c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe), in a patient with clinical and molecular diagnosis of the syndrome [21: "The molecular analysis of a DNA sample taken from peripheral blood lymphocytes revealed the germinal mutation c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe) on exon 5 of the TP53 gene"].

## Clinical And Phenotypic Variability

Clinical presentation varies widely even among carriers of the same TP53 pathogenic variant, and this heterogeneity may be shaped by TP53 mutation type, related polymorphic variants, copy number variation, or epigenetic regulation of TP53 expression [22: "TP53 type mutation, polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions, and/or epigenetic deregulation of TP53 expression might be responsible for clinical heterogeneity"].

## Research And Clinical Activity

The condition is actively studied through literature indexed under Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [7], multiple PubMed reviews and reports [5][10][13][16], and dedicated clinical studies such as Role of p53 Gene in Metabolism Regulation in Patients With Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [11], Clinical and Genetic Studies of Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [17], and LIFSCREEN : Evaluation of Whole Body MRI for Early Detection of Cancers in Subjects With P53 Mutation (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome) [20].

Li-Fraumeni syndrome is associated with three genes in the graph: NCBIGene:1029, cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1]; NCBIGene:11200, checkpoint kinase 2 [3]; and NCBIGene:7157, tumor protein p53 [4], all linked to the disease record named Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2].

## Core gene association

TP53, the tumor protein p53 gene, is the principal driver, since the syndrome is caused by a germline mutation of this gene on chromosome 17p13.1 with autosomal dominant, highly penetrant inheritance [19: "Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1"]. Loss of p53 function through TP53 mutation permits development of multiple malignancies including sarcomas, osteosarcoma, premenopausal breast cancer, brain tumors, and adrenal cortical carcinomas [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53, leading to downstream events permissive for development of various malignancies throughout life"]. A confirmed case report likewise identified the germline mutation c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe) in exon 5 of the TP53 gene as the deleterious cause in a patient with confirmed molecular diagnosis [21: "revealed the germinal mutation c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe) on exon 5 of the TP53 gene, a deleterious mutation described previously in tumoural tissues"].

## Clinical heterogeneity and modifiers

Phenotypic variability among carriers of the same TP53 pathogenic variant, and even within the same family, is attributed in part to TP53 mutation type, polymorphic variants in TP53 or related genes, copy number variation, and epigenetic regulation of TP53 expression [22: "TP53 type mutation, polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions, and/or epigenetic deregulation of TP53 expression might be responsible for clinical heterogeneity"].

## Literature and identifiers

The disease is indexed under the MedGen title Li-Fraumeni syndrome [6] and appears in the literature entity index as Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [7]. Relevant PubMed titles include Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [5], Li-Fraumeni syndrome. [10], Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [13], and Li-Fraumeni syndrome heterogeneity. [16], corresponding to publications with PMID 27617148 [9], PMID 27622479 [12], PMID 30333936 [15], and PMID 31691207 [18].

## Related clinical trials

Registered trials touching this syndrome include Clinical, Genetic, Behavioral, Laboratory and Epidemiologic Characterization of Individuals and Families at High Risk of Breast/Ovarian Cancer [8], Role of p53 Gene in Metabolism Regulation in Patients With Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [11], Characterization of Patients With Uncommon Presentations and/or Uncommon Diseases Associated With the Cardiovascular System [14], Clinical and Genetic Studies of Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [17], and LIFSCREEN : Evaluation of Whole Body MRI for Early Detection of Cancers in Subjects With P53 Mutation (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome) [20].
